Step Name:Calendar table
Detailed Instructions:
On Power BI desktop under Modeling click on New table button
Type the Dax formula below in the Dax formula bar, Click on the check mark, and save
Calendar = ADDCOLUMNS(
    CALENDARAUTO(),
    "Year", Year([Date]),
    "Month Number", Month([Date]),
    "Month Name Short", FORMAT([Date], "MMM"),
    "HolidayName",
    SWITCH(
        TRUE(),
        Month([Date]) = 1, "New Years",
        Month([Date]) = 2, "Super Bowl",
        Month([Date]) = 9, "Labor Day",
        Month([Date]) = 11, "Thanksgiving",
        Month([Date]) = 12, "Christmas",
        BLANK()  // Default case if no holiday matches
    )
)

Refresh Date Table
On Power BI Desktop ribbon, Click on Transform data
Click on New Source button, and select Blank query from the list and click on Connect
Under properties in the Name box type in 'Refresh Date'
On the Dax formula bar type ' =Date Time.LocalNow()'
Click on Convert to Table button 
After the refresh table pops up, rename the column by right clicking and choosing rename from the selection
Click  on Close & apply button and save

Step Name:Create DAX measures
Detailed Instructions:
Select the Walmart Table under the fields pane by clicking on it 
From Power BI desktop ribbon, Home tab click on New measure 
The formula bar appears along the top of the report canvas. 
 Fill in all the DAX formulas provided below, one at a time, and when you finish Press Enter or select Commit (checkmark icon) in the formula bar.  

After creating each measure choose the necessary format and decimal for each value (measure)
Save
DAX Formulas
.Arrow YOY CPI = SWITCH(TRUE(), [.CPI YOY] <0, UNICHAR(9662),[.CPI YOY] =0, UNICHAR(9666), UNICHAR(9652))

.Arrow YOY% = SWITCH(TRUE(), [.Sales YOY] <0, UNICHAR(9662),[.Sales YOY] =0, UNICHAR(9666), UNICHAR(9652))

.AVG CPI = AVERAGE(WalmartSales[CPI_x])

.AVG Sales = AVERAGE(WalmartSales[Weekly_Sales])

.CPI YOY = 
VAR CurrentYearValue = [.AVG CPI]
VAR PreviousYearValue = CALCULATE([.AVG CPI], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Calendar'[Date]))

RETURN
    IF(
        CurrentYearValue = 0,
        BLANK(),  -- or you can replace this with any other value or calculation
        DIVIDE(CurrentYearValue - PreviousYearValue, PreviousYearValue)
    )

.Sales Per Month = DIVIDE([.Total Sales],DISTINCTCOUNT('Calendar'[Month Name Short]),0)+0

.Sales YOY = 
VAR CurrentYearValue = [.AVG Sales]
VAR PreviousYearValue = CALCULATE([.AVG Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Calendar'[Date]))

RETURN
    IF(
        CurrentYearValue = 0,
        BLANK(),  -- or you can replace this with any other value or calculation
        DIVIDE(CurrentYearValue - PreviousYearValue, PreviousYearValue)
    )

.Total Sales = SUM(WalmartSales[Weekly_Sales])

AVG Holiday sales = AVERAGE(WalmartSales[holidaysales])

AVG non Holiday sales = AVERAGE(WalmartSales[Non holidaysales])

HolidayInc% = 
VAR HolidayPeriods = VALUES('WalmartSales'[Specific_US_Holiday])
VAR AverageNonHolidaySales = CALCULATE(
    AVERAGE('WalmartSales'[Non holidaysales]),
    ALL('WalmartSales'), // Removes any existing row context, but you might adjust this to respect certain filters.
    'WalmartSales'[Specific_US_Holiday] = "Non holiday" // Focuses on non-holiday sales.
)
RETURN
    AVERAGEX(
        HolidayPeriods,
        VAR HolidaySales = CALCULATE(
            AVERAGE('WalmartSales'[holidaysales]),
            'WalmartSales'[Specific_US_Holiday] = EARLIER('WalmartSales'[Specific_US_Holiday])
        )
        RETURN
            IF(
                HolidaySales <> 0,
                DIVIDE(HolidaySales - AverageNonHolidaySales, AverageNonHolidaySales),
                BLANK()
            )
    )

WeeklySales = CALCULATE(AVERAGE(WalmartSales[holidaysales]) + AVERAGE(WalmartSales[Non holidaysales])) / 2 

YoY Growth = 
VAR CurrentYearValue = [WeeklySales]
VAR PreviousYearValue = CALCULATE([WeeklySales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Calendar'[Date]))

RETURN
IF(
    ISBLANK(PreviousYearValue) || PreviousYearValue = 0,
    BLANK(),
    IF(
        (CurrentYearValue - PreviousYearValue) / PreviousYearValue = -1,
        BLANK(),
        (CurrentYearValue - PreviousYearValue) / PreviousYearValue
    )
)

portfolioContent.title: The Effect of Holiday Sales on Walmart Using ML
portfolioContent.portfolioSummary: Developed a Power BI and machine learning solution analyzing holiday impacts on Walmart sales from 2010 to 2012.
portfolioContent.summary: This project analyzed Walmart sales data from 2010 to 2012 to understand the effect of holidays on sales performance using Power BI and machine learning techniques. It involved data import, transformation, DAX measure creation, and dashboard visualization to deliver actionable insights. The solution enabled clear visualization of sales trends and holiday impacts for strategic decision-making.
portfolioContent.businessProblem: Walmart needed to understand how holiday periods influenced their sales to optimize inventory and marketing strategies. Without clear insights, the company risked inefficient resource allocation during key sales periods. The project aimed to quantify and visualize these holiday effects to support better business planning.
objectives: Import and prepare Walmart sales data for analysis in Power BI
Create calculated columns and DAX measures to identify holiday impacts
Develop an interactive dashboard to visualize sales trends during holidays
workflow: Import Walmart sales CSV data into Power BI Desktop
Create calendar and conditional columns to flag holidays
Establish relationships between sales and calendar tables
Develop DAX measures to calculate sales and CPI year-over-year changes
Design and deploy a comprehensive Power BI dashboard with logos and titles
keyInsights: Holiday periods such as Christmas and Thanksgiving significantly increase Walmart sales.
Sales trends show distinct seasonal patterns aligned with major holidays from 2010 to 2012.
Unemployment rate and CPI metrics were integrated to contextualize sales performance.
Custom sorting and conditional columns improved clarity in holiday sales analysis.
businessImpact: Enabled Walmart to optimize inventory and marketing efforts during peak holiday seasons.
Provided stakeholders with clear visual insights to support strategic sales planning.
Improved decision-making through integrated economic indicators and sales data.
